note: Which vendor posts to read, whose models each post may speak for, and which of its benchmark labels correspond to ours. Every mapping here is a human-reviewable decision rather than something the extractor guesses.
own_models_only: A vendor's post usually tabulates competitors alongside its own models. A number OpenAI publishes under a Claude column is OpenAI's claim about Anthropic's model, not Anthropic's claim about it, and recording it as a vendor_claim for Anthropic would misattribute it. Only columns belonging to the post's own publisher are extracted; every other column is counted and reported, never stored.
columns_note: A column is only mapped when it names the same variant our score row was measured on. Our openai-gpt-5.5 row is the Pro variant, so a post column reading plainly 'GPT-5.5' is a DIFFERENT model and is left unmapped rather than credited to it - the kind of near-miss that produces a confident comparison between two things that were never the same.

GPQA Diamond.note: Same benchmark and same slice Epoch measures. Both are single-number accuracy on the Diamond subset.

FrontierMath Tier 1-3 (v2).reason: A tier subset of FrontierMath v2. Epoch's frontiermath scores the full set, so the two numbers describe different question pools and differencing them would invent a gap out of a definitional mismatch.

FrontierMath Tier 4 (v2).reason: The hardest tier of FrontierMath v2 alone, against Epoch's full-set score. Not the same measurement.

comparability_rule: A delta is only computed when the label is marked comparable AND the configuration matches: the post's column has to describe the same variant our score row was measured on. Epoch measures a specific effort level, recorded per score row, and a vendor reporting a different one is publishing a different number rather than a contradictory one.
gap_threshold_note: |vendor - third_party| / third_party. Set in the anti-bias rules; a smaller difference is within the noise of two independent runs of the same benchmark.
